article.title: How to Fix a Sliding Patio Door That Drags
article.summary: Make a sliding patio door glide again: clean and straighten the track, lubricate it with silicone, and raise the rollers with their adjustment screws.
article.body:
A sliding glass door that drags, grinds or needs two hands usually has a dirty track or rollers that have dropped. Both are quick fixes. This guide covers standard sliding patio doors with adjustable bottom rollers.

Affiliate disclosure: some links in this guide are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. We only recommend products we'd use ourselves.

Safety: sliding glass panels are very heavy. Don't lift a panel off its track by yourself; that's a two-person job, and roller replacement usually requires it.

Steps

  1. Clean the track thoroughly

    Open the door fully and vacuum the bottom track, then scrub it with a stiff brush and an all-purpose cleaner. Close the door and clean the other half of the track. Dirt packed into the track is the most common cause of dragging.

    Done right: the track is clean along its full length on both sides of the door.

  2. Check the track for dents

    Run a fingertip along the raised rail the rollers ride on. A dent or bent spot makes the door bump. Gently straighten small bends with pliers, using a block of wood to protect the rail.

    Done right: the rail feels straight and smooth along its whole length.

  3. Lubricate with silicone, not grease

    Spray a light coat of dry silicone lubricant on the track rail and the rollers you can reach. Wipe off excess. Oil and grease attract dirt and make the problem come back.

    Done right: the track feels slick, not sticky.

  4. Adjust the rollers

    Look for small holes or caps on the bottom edge of the door panel at each end; behind them are the roller adjustment screws. Turn each screw a quarter turn at a time, usually clockwise to raise the door, and slide the door between adjustments. Raise both ends until the door glides and the gap at the top is even.

    Done right: the door slides with one finger and the gap along the frame is even top to bottom.

  5. Check the lock and latch

    Close the door and test the lock. Raising the door can change where the latch hits the strike. Adjust the strike on the frame if the lock doesn't catch easily.

    Done right: the door locks without lifting or pushing it.

Call a door technician if: the rollers are cracked or seized and the panel needs to come out, the glass is damaged, or the door frame is out of square. Replacing rollers means lifting a very heavy glass panel.

FAQ

Why is my sliding door so hard to open?

Most often the track is dirty or the rollers have dropped so the door rides on the frame. Cleaning and adjusting the rollers fixes most cases.

What lubricant is best for sliding doors?

A dry silicone spray. Avoid oil and grease, which attract dirt.

Where are the adjustment screws on a sliding door?

Usually in small holes, often under caps, on the bottom edge of the door panel at each end.

Can I replace sliding door rollers myself?

It's possible, but the panel must be lifted out of the frame, which takes two people. Many homeowners hire a door technician.
